title: Villains v1
description: The `villains` block a finished world carries. It describes what the generator emits today and does not design anything: every property here was read off Sim/icarus_sim/terrain_villains.py rather than proposed. A world built with `villain_rise: 0` carries no block at all, so absence is a legal state of a world and not a failure of this contract. Tier is a continuous reach and `super villain` is a band on it rather than a flag: SUPER_TIER is 1.0, a reign is held above `villain_hold`, and the simulation's final age promotes the most concentrated regions to exactly SUPER_TIER so a generated world ends with antagonists standing in it. `people` holds everyone who ever held a region, living and fallen, the same shape `heroes.people` uses for legends and `npcs.people` for the dead: one list, a status field, and the reader filters. Every consumer that means "who stands right now" must say so, and absent status reads as living so older records still resolve.

tiers.description: Accumulated tier per region anchor, the thing that actually persists. A villain is the name the world puts on a region that has concentrated past the band; the region outlives the villain. Keys are ley node ids, or `seat-<city uid>` where a world has no magic at all, and never culture ids -- a culture's id is rebuilt every age from whatever the roads join, so tier keyed to one silently resets and nothing can ever reach the band. A villain's own well is excluded from anchor selection, because a region anchored to its holder's work is anchored to something that did not exist before that holder.

people.description: Everyone who ever held a region, living first by anchor and then the fallen in the order they fell. A region may hold both a fallen villain and the successor that replaced it, so `region` is not unique across this list.

uid.description: `villain-<age>-<terrain node>`. Keyed to the age it rose and the terrain node it rose on, never to a settlement ordinal: hamlet, fortress, plot and nest ids are all renumbered on every age advance.

region.description: The region anchor this villain holds, matching a key of `tiers`.

seat_uid.description: The city uid it rose in. A city uid is stable across ages; its position in `settlements.sites` is not.

node.description: Terrain node index of the seat.

school.description: The magic school of the nearest ley node, or null in a world with no magic.

god.description: Present once a school-bound villain has been given its god; a well is only sunk by a villain that has one.

held_nodes.description: Ley node ids this villain holds, including its own well once sunk.

tier.description: Continuous standing. At or above 1.0 is the super band; a pretender stalled by a full ceiling sits at 0.999.

reach_m.description: tier x 4 x settlement_spacing. A field with falloff, not a radius of control.

growth.description: Which pressure raised it, and therefore the counter-play. Derived from the region's dominant threat.

status.description: Whether this villain still holds its region. Read through terrain_villains.standing(); absent reads as living.

well.description: The leyline well a god-bound villain sank: a source that is joined, so the edges are the point.

claims.description: Ground this villain took. Claims persist after a fall -- held ground outlives its holder -- and each one carries its holder's state so a consumer reads how hard it presses off the claim itself rather than joining against the roster.

log.description: What happened to this villain and when. `promoted` is the terminal pass that seats a region as the simulation ends; `rose` is accumulation crossing the band during an age.

fallen.description: The durable mark of a reign that actually changed the world, in the same shape a ruined city gets one in `ruins`: appended, never pruned. A villain that reached the band, took no city, staked no claim and sank no well gets no record here -- that is a condition, not a formality. `tier` and `reach_m` are deliberately absent: both describe a grip it no longer has. The mark carries no asset_id, because a fallen villain's holdings are already placed.

left.description: What it did to the world, read back out of `ruins` and its own claims rather than accumulated on the record, because anything hung on a live record is lost the moment that record is rebuilt.

works.description: What seated villains built this age, present only in an age that built something. Written after the rebuild, on settled ground: a well joins the holdings a villain actually has this age and a claim names the peoples actually near it.

outlook.description: Where turmoil is concentrating, so a story layer need not guess. The counterpart of war_outlook: that one tells "they are coming" from "we once fought", this one separates a region about to produce something from one that is merely violent.

ceiling.description: ceil(regions / villain_density), at least one. How many may stand in the band at once.

standing.description: Must equal the number of rows below with `seated` true, and the number of living entries in `people`.

stalled.description: At or above the stall line but refused a seat because the ceiling is full. Succession, with no succession system.
